note: Every dataset the app uses, where it comes from, and what its licence allows. Check the licence before adding a source here. Nothing that needs a publisher's permission is listed until that permission is in hand.

sources.name: King James Version
sources.provides: The full Bible text, 66 books, 1,189 chapters
sources.licence: Public domain in the United States
sources.notes: Public domain in the United States; in the United Kingdom the KJV is under perpetual Crown copyright, administered by Cambridge University Press. This edition was chosen over another because it keeps the small-capital LORD that renders the divine name (5,621 verses, against 6 in the edition tried first) and spells place names without dashes, which stopped them matching.

sources.name: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible
sources.provides: The Hebrew text of the Old Testament, tagged word by word with lemma and morphology
sources.notes: Attribution required. Credit goes in the app's About screen.

sources.name: SBL Greek New Testament (MorphGNT)
sources.provides: The Greek text of the New Testament, tagged word by word with lemma and parsing
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 for the morphological tagging; the SBLGNT text under the SBLGNT licence
sources.notes: Attribution required. Credited in the app.

sources.name: Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs (TBESH and TBESG)
sources.provides: What each Hebrew and Greek dictionary entry means: headword, transliteration, gloss and definition
sources.notes: From STEPBible. Attribution required and credited in the app. 9,250 Hebrew and 5,025 Greek entries are used, matched to the entries the texts actually carry; the rest are mostly proper names.

sources.name: Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References (TIPNR)
sources.provides: Every person and place in Scripture as an individual, with their family, and every verse where each is named
sources.notes: From STEPBible and Tyndale House Cambridge. Attribution required and credited in the app. Their licence asks that copies of the file not be posted elsewhere, so it is downloaded at build time and only derived data is kept. It identifies individuals rather than names, which is what lets the reader tell Mary the mother of Jesus from Mary Magdalene. Each claim is checked against the King James text before it is kept: 28,426 of 31,718 survive, the rest being names this translation spells differently or does not carry. The file also holds longer descriptions written by an AI in 2024 and since adapted; those are deliberately not used.

sources.name: OpenBible.info geocoding
sources.provides: Where each place is now, how confident the identification is, coordinates, and a photograph of the site
sources.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for the data; each photograph under its own licence
sources.notes: Matched to TIPNR's places by the verses they share, or by TIPNR's own identifier where OpenBible records it. Photographs marked 'copyright' are never used; the rest are downloaded once at build time, credited on each profile, and bundled so they work offline.

sources.name: Theographic Bible Metadata
sources.provides: For each person and place, the paragraph of Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897, public domain) about that individual, a disambiguated title, other names, and estimated dates
sources.notes: Matched to TIPNR's individuals by the share of verses they have in common, one to one within a name, so the thirty Zechariahs each get their own entry rather than the prophet's. Share-alike applies to the derived profiles file.

sources.name: Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons
sources.provides: Portraits of well-known people, chosen in data/portraits.json
sources.licence: Public domain or Creative Commons, per image
sources.notes: Each chosen person's English Wikipedia article is followed to its Wikidata item and the image Wikidata gives (P18). Only freely licensed images are kept, with the artist and licence shown on the profile. Anyone without one shows 'No portrait known'.

sources.name: OpenBible cross-references (Treasury of Scripture Knowledge)
sources.provides: Where else Scripture says this: 193,436 references across 29,324 verses, ranked by how many readers thought each link a good one
sources.notes: Built on the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge, which is public domain, and ranked by reader votes. Attribution required and credited in the app. openbible.info cannot be reached from the build, so the data is downloaded from scrollmapper/bible_databases, an MIT-licensed collection that carries it unchanged. Of 344,799 links, only those readers voted up are kept, and at most eight for any one verse: a verse offering forty references is less useful than one offering eight, because the reader has to weigh them all.

excluded.note: These translations need written permission from their publisher before any of their text can go in the app. Until then the app links out to them. See docs/data-licenses.md.
